subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: The Diesel Engine: Ignition by Compression
description: One-minute skill: The Diesel Engine: Ignition by Compression.

hook.text: What if fuel ignites with no spark at all? Rudolf Diesel made it work.

buildup.text: Compress air hot enough and injected fuel ignites on contact. No spark plug.

discovery.text: Higher compression ratios mean more efficiency. Diesel beats gasoline there.

twist.text: Diesel's first engine exploded during testing. It took years to get right.

climax.text: Diesels now power nearly all trucks, ships, trains, and generators.

punchline.text: Squeeze air hard enough and it lights the fuel itself.

quiz.question: Why are diesel engines more efficient than gasoline engines?
options: Diesel fuel contains more energy per liter than gasoline
Higher compression ratios extract more work from each combustion cycle
Diesel engines have fewer moving parts and less friction
